title: Status Process Summary: Functionality

children:
The system uses statuses to determine at what stage of processing an entity currently is at in your warehouse. Statuses for inbound processing identify the current processing state 
 of a receipt or receipt line; statuses for outbound execution perform 
 this task for a shipment or a shipment line. For both functional 
 areas, the status is defined on the line. As different processes 
 are committed against that line, its status changes. The header 
 record, either the receipt or the shipment, identifies the most and least 
 advanced statuses assigned to its lines. This allows you to quickly 
 assess the general status of the entire receipt or shipment.

A status flow is a defined sequence of statuses grouped together to 
 manage processing. It determines which procedures will be completed against 
 a specific line record (receipt, shipment). Status flows are defined 
 at the line level; this allows you to accommodate item level 
 requirements.
 
When the system processes a flow, it executes each status (number) in 
 sequential order. For example, status 100 is completed before status 101. 
 The system will require that a status is completed before a new one is 
 initiated.

All status flows are assigned at the line level. If it 
 is not defined, the system will assign the default flow.

When a detail is interfaced to the system, the system will determine 
 how its processed based on its status flow.
The system will process the line through the statuses in the flow.

As the line is processed, the system will update its "parent" entity (receipt/shipment) to 
 reflect is progress. These records include two status fields: the 
 Trailing Status Field and the Leading Status Field.

As the shipment's/receipt's containers move through the functional 
 area's major processes, the system cycles through the statuses.

The default status flow is automatically assigned to all line 
 records (for shipments and receipts) that are not associated with a custom 
 status flow. Therefore, the default status flow should accommodate the 
 majority of products that you process.
Below are all of the Inbound Processing default statuses:

(100) Check 
 In Pending: The receipt has arrived at the warehouse and is awaiting 
 check in.

(200) Locate 
 Pending: The units on at least one receipt line were checked 
 in. The container(s) created during check in are awaiting locating.

(300) Putaway 
 Pending: The containers were located and work creation generated 
 putaway instructions for them. The containers are awaiting work execution 
 to be called. The containers are brought to their storage locations during 
 work execution.

(301) In Putaway: 
 Work creation generated putaway instructions for the container(s). Someone 
 has begun transporting the container(s) from the receiving dock to the 
 storage location(s) selected during locating.

(900) Closed: 
 All receipt lines for this receipt have been checked in and located. 
 If the work creation was called, the container(s) have been physically 
 moved to storage location(s).                  If work 
 creation was not called, locating has selected storage locations for the 
 container(s). In other words, if you do not require work creation, the 
 container will move from status 200 to status 900, provided no custom 
 default statuses are not added.
Below are all of the Outbound Execution default statuses:

(90) In Pool Pending: The shipment's status before it is processed via the interface. The purpose of this status is to be a temporary status used by the interface download process to ensure that shipments do not get picked up for processing while the interface process is running. Also, shipments in this status cannot be added to a wave.

(100) In Pool: 
 The shipment has not been processed in a wave, but has been created in the pool or downloaded via the interface. No work can be performed 
 against this shipment.

(200) Wave Pending: 
 The wave is being built. It has not been run.

(201) In Wave: 
 A wave run was initiated and the wave has not been released.

(300) Picking 
 Pending: A wave was released, but none of the work has been initiated.

(301) In Picking: 
 At least one work instruction associated with this shipment has been assigned 
 to an employee.

(400) Packing 
 Pending: At least one work instruction associated with this shipment 
 has been pick confirmed. It can now be packed.

(401) In Packing: 
 At least one work instruction associated with this shipment has been packed.

(600) Staging 
 Pending: All items of a shipment have been picked, packed, and/or 
 consolidated.

(650) Loading 
 Pending: All items of a shipment have been picked, packed, or consolidated, 
 and/or staged.

(700) Ship Confirm 
 Pending: At least one container associated with this shipment has 
 been closed.

(800) Load Confirm 
 Pending: All shipments on the load have been ship confirmed and 
 the load is ready to be confirmed.

(900) Closed: 
 The shipping load has been confirmed.

(990) Delivered: 
 A shipment or parcel has been delivered to it's intended recipient through 
 the system.

(994) Complete 
 Rejected To Pool: System uses this in the status action to indicate 
 that if the entire shipment cannot be allocated it will send it back to 
 the pool.

(995) Finished 
 Item Is Allocated: Assigned to a component line when its parent 
 item has been allocated by the system.

(996) Component 
 Item Is Allocated: Assigned to a parent item when the system could 
 not allocate it, but all of its component item(s) were allocated.

(997) Immediate 
 Need Pending: There is at least one shipment line that is ties 
 to an outstanding immediate need.

(998) Delete 
 Rejected: A quantity on a shipment line was rejected. The 
 quantity will be deleted from the system.

(999) Rejected: 
 During allocation, if any quantity on the line is rejected, this status 
 will indicate that rejected quantity.

The system also supports custom statuses, which are created especially for your specific business processes. Like a default status, a custom 
 status is a process committed against either a shipment or a receipt, 
 based on functional area.

A custom status flow allows you to address unique processing requirements 
 for a specific line. It must be associated with the line record before 
 its interfaced to the system. Although its assigned before the line
 is interfaced, this flow must also be defined in the system on the Custom 
 Status Flow Window. Custom status flows can accommodate any value on either the top level or 
 line level. For example, many companies create a custom outbound execution 
 status flow to accommodate emergency or rush orders. If the shipment line identifies the "Rush" flow in the Status Flow Field, this line (and 
 its containers) will be processed using this custom status flow. A rush custom status flow probably does not require new statuses. Instead, 
 it includes fewer statuses than the default status flow to streamline 
 processing for time sensitive shipments or receipts. As the line is processed through the system, the system updates the 
 top level record's trailing and leading status values. If this line is the least 
 advanced line for the entity (receipt or detail), its status will be 
 the header's trailing status.

These values are defined on the top level record (receipt/shipment). The 
 trailing status is the least advanced status associated with the record; 
 the leading status is the most advanced status associated with the record. 
 The system obtains this information from the containers created for the 
 entity. You can use this information to research container activity and 
 perform troubleshooting tasks.
